# Ahmed Mahrous

> Academic research in artificial intelligence, learning, strategic behavior, and decentralized financial systems. These are Markdown versions of the public website, generated from its HTML.

## Research publications

- [The reflexivity threshold: A phase transition for multi-agent performative prediction](https://amahrous.com/papers/reflexivity-threshold/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous and Roberto Di Pietro. NeurIPS 2026 · Accepted, 2026. Under the stated sensitivity and curvature assumptions, a reflexivity matrix with spectral radius below one guarantees convergence of repeated retraining. Above one, we construct noisy systems where every local-information learner incurs expected cumulative excess loss growing linearly for horizons up to order 1/(ρ(Γ) − 1).
- [Stablecoins: Fundamentals, emerging issues, and open challenges](https://amahrous.com/papers/stablecoins/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous, Maurantonio Caprolu, and Roberto Di Pietro. International Review of Economics & Finance, 111, 105665, 2026. A systematic review of stablecoin research, connecting economic, technical, and policy questions and identifying open challenges.
- [FinMoji: A framework for emoji-driven sentiment analysis in financial social media](https://amahrous.com/papers/finmoji/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous, Jens Schneider, and Roberto Di Pietro. ACM Transactions on the Web, 20(3), Article 35, 2026. On about 528,000 emoji-containing StockTwits posts, emoji-only sentiment models reach F1 ≈ 0.75, versus ≈ 0.88 for text-and-emoji models, with substantially lower computational cost. Financial emoji usage also differs from general social-media usage.
- [Cross-cultural transfer of emoji semantics and sentiment in financial social media](https://amahrous.com/papers/cross-cultural-emojis/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous and Roberto Di Pietro. Findings of ACL 2026, 2026. Across financial communities in four languages, emoji frequencies vary while meanings and sentiment polarity remain largely stable. Including emojis reduces sentiment-transfer gaps relative to text-only models, though cross-language transfer remains the hardest setting.
- [What prediction-market contracts reveal at launch: Trading volume and dispute risk](https://amahrous.com/papers/prediction-market-launch/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous and Roberto Di Pietro. ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF 2026), 2026. Across 802,863 resolved Polymarket markets, launch-time contract information predicts trading activity, but demand prediction weakens sharply across periods of platform change. Dispute scores help rank groups of markets; the low dispute rate limits predictions for individual contracts.
- [PumpSense: Real-time detection and target extraction of crypto pump-and-dumps on Telegram](https://amahrous.com/papers/pumpsense/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous and Roberto Di Pietro. IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Cryptocurrency (ICBC 2026), 2026. Using over 280,000 Telegram posts, we benchmark pump-announcement detection and extraction of the target coin and exchange. LightGBM reaches F1 = 0.79 and BGE-M3 reaches 0.83; LLMs perform best on target extraction.
- [TSTR for financial fraud: Learning to detect manipulation without real data](https://amahrous.com/papers/tstr-financial-fraud/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous and Roberto Di Pietro. ACM International Conference on AI in Finance (ICAIF 2025), 2025. A classifier trained only on synthetic pump-and-dump time series achieves 79.75% accuracy on real data. Adding 20% real training data raises accuracy to 88.1%, while simple Gaussian sampling outperforms the deep generative models tested.
- [SoK: A structured analysis of economic and technical stablecoin-related research](https://amahrous.com/papers/stablecoin-sok/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous, Maurantonio Caprolu, and Roberto Di Pietro. IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Cryptocurrency (ICBC 2025), 2025. A structured account of economic and technical research on stablecoins.
- [Demystifying the role of aesthetics in NFT pricing: Model, analysis, and insights](https://amahrous.com/papers/nft-aesthetics/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous and Roberto Di Pietro. International Conference on Blockchain Computing and Applications (BCCA 2025), 2025. Across over 160,000 NFTs in 32 collections, collection identity inflates apparent visual price predictability. Controlling for it leaves weak generalization across collections, although visual features retain modest predictive power within some collections.
- [What drives cryptocurrency pump and dump schemes: Coin versus market factors?](https://amahrous.com/papers/pump-and-dump/index.md): Lanouar Charfeddine and Ahmed Mahrous. Finance Research Letters, 67, 105861, 2024. An empirical study of coin-level and market-level factors associated with cryptocurrency pump-and-dump schemes.
- [The role of emojis in sentiment analysis of financial microblogs](https://amahrous.com/papers/financial-microblog-emojis/index.md): Ahmed Mahrous, Jens Schneider, and Roberto Di Pietro. Fourth International Conference on Intelligent Data Science Technologies and Applications (IDSTA 2023), 2023. A study of emojis in sentiment analysis of financial microblogs.
